thread:
maya: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel swap (rolled ~1718604000) we're seeing p95 regressions on a couple of routes. free tier /chat-complete p95 went 85ms -> 160ms, pro /embed-large 70ms -> 130ms. kv hitrate dropped ~6%. wondering if the continuous-batcher heuristics are overshooting token budgets and tripping a slower kernel path.

sam: can you paste the short profiler output and the batcher config that was active during the spike? also which kernel got selected? @lucas FYI.

lucas: copying what I saw in the flame output this morning — looked like more microbatch boundary stalls and kernel fallback events. here's a trimmed profiler snippet from the canary harness: 

```
PROFILE SUMMARY (canary run 03/15):
route: /chat-complete (tier=free)
avg_batch_size: 4.3 -> 6.1
median_tokens_per_req: 32
token_budget_target (effective): 128 (we set dynamic -> default high)
kernel_selected: optimized_attn_v2 -> fallback_generic when seq>512
kernel_latency_p50/p95: 10ms / 95ms  -> 12ms / 190ms
kv_cache_hits/sec: 240 -> 225
microbatch_wait_time p95: 6ms -> 28ms
```
\nmaya: thanks. the important bits are: token_budget_target spiked for that route after the new default policy, and kernel selection shifted for some seq-length combos. guess is larger batches + high token budgets causing different kernel path + kv churn.

sam: two immediate experiments: 1) lower token_budget_target for free routes to 64; 2) change queue policy to favor short-payload, low-token requests so they don't aggregate into big microbatches. also consider enabling kv_prefetch for embed route.

lucas: agree. proposed quick patch to batcher config (small, canary-friendly):

```
# patch snippet for canary
routes:
  /chat-complete:
    token_budget_target: 64
    queue_policy: short-first
    kernel_hint: prefer_attn_v1
  /embed-large:
    token_budget_target: 96
    kv_prefetch: true
canary:
  pct: 5
  duration: 2h
```
\nana: (typo — ana) add these metrics to the canary dashboard and alert if any of them cross thresholds: p95_latency > +25% from baseline, kv_hit_rate drops > 4%, error_rate > 0.5%. prometheus queries: 

- p95_latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- kv_hit_rate: sum(rate(kv_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_lookups_total[5m]))
- microbatch_wait_p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(microbatch_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

maya: canary plan sounds good. i'll kick off 5% canary, 2h window. sam you own runbook monitoring? lucas please attach perf harness command so QA can reproduce.

lucas: repro command I used (perf harness):
```
./perf_harness --route /chat-complete --concurrency 16 --seed 42 --profile --duration 300
```
reproduces the p95 regression within ~2-3 runs. also dump attached: `profiling/171860_harness_dump.tar.gz` (uploaded to /mnt/ci).

infra-bot: deploy job created: deploy-7891 (canary patch). ETA ~6m. link: https://ci.redwood/prod/deploy-7891 :gear:

sam: I'll watch the dashboard and mute noisy alerts. escalation: if p95 > +40% or error_rate spikes, we rollback to previous kernel defaults and token_budget_target=128 for free routes.

maya: running canary now. will post short updates every 15m. thanks team. :thumbsup:

lucas: note for later — we should add a kernel-affinity heuristic to prefer attn_v1 for sequences < 256 and v2 only for heavy long seq work; also bake that into the batcher so kernel decisions happen before microbatching completes. reduces expensive fallbacks.

ana: added dashboard panels and synthetic probe.

maya: update 15m: canary is live at 5% — initial p95 looks steady (down to baseline for the canary cohort). kv hit_rate unchanged so far. continuing watches.

sam: +1 monitoring, will update if anything trips.

maya: update 1h30: canary holding. p95 for canary cohort ~ baseline, broader traffic still affected until we cut a global rollout. propose staged rollout + kernel-affinity change in next patch.

lucas: i'll PR the kernel-affinity proposal and bench it in harness. thanks everyone.

maya: closing the thread for now; we'll follow up in eng-runtime weekly with the kernel-affinity RFC. :white_check_mark:
